Reliable financial information shapes decisions, protects businesses, and helps them act in a way that is both financially responsible and trustworthy. That is what drew me to financial accounting and continues to shape the way I approach it. I am from India, and I hold a Bachelor’s degree from a university not listed in the major global rankings. My interest in this field grew from a genuine curiosity about how organisations operate and from seeing how much value can be added when reporting figures is reflected in everyday work. I am especially drawn to the point where careful analysis meets practical action, because accurate reporting supports confidence from both the business and its customers. That connection became especially personal during a family dinner in the middle of year-end reporting, when I explained how balance sheets work using the restaurant bill; the conversation quickly turned into a lively debate about who counted as an “asset” to the family, and it stayed with me because it showed how accounting can quietly support decisions and relationships.

My academic background and project work have given me a practical foundation for this path. Across my experience, I have completed 4 projects with tangible outcomes, each requiring me to turn complex figures into clear, usable information that supported decisions. In one role, I needed to use a new technique that the work required; within a couple of months I had learned it well enough to apply it independently in my own tasks. On another project, a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing the team down, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped the work move forward more smoothly. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas they know I have worked on before, and I value those moments because they reflect the importance of clear communication and dependable support. I also took the initiative to begin a substantial piece of work beyond my formal role and carried it through over many months until it was completed.

Overall, I am eager to bring this foundation to a Financial Accountant role, contributing accurate reporting, strong controls, and dependable financial insight in a setting where sound decisions matter.

Few things are more rewarding than watching a child move from uncertainty to understanding, and that is what drew me towards becoming a Primary School Teacher. I chose this path because I want to help children build confidence through learning and to make the classroom a place where curiosity, fairness, and encouragement can grow alongside the ability to participate, communicate, and build a positive, life-changing foundation for the rest of a child’s development. Originally from Colombia, I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 100, and across my work I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes. One of those experiences strengthened my commitment to this profession: I saw how much difference clear, engaging teaching can make when children are not only exposed to new ideas, but encouraged to participate, ask questions, and make sense of what is presented.

My academic and professional development has been shaped by practical experience. In one role, I needed to use a new technique that the work required; within a couple of months I had learned it well enough to apply it independently in my own tasks. On another occasion, I noticed that the team was repeatedly losing time at the same stage of a process, so I introduced a simple adjustment that reduced the delay and made the work smoother. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas they know I have worked on, and I value those moments because they reflect the importance of clear communication and steady support. I also volunteered for a major undertaking outside my formal duties and continued it alongside my regular work for over a year until it was completed.

What keeps this profession personal for me is the human side of learning. One of my favourite memories is a school reading event where a younger family member proudly introduced me as “the teacher who makes stories come alive.” That moment captured exactly why I want to contribute as a Primary School Teacher: to turn curiosity into confidence, create inclusive lessons that invite participation, and help children feel seen, capable, and excited to come to school.

Precision has always appealed to me, especially when careful testing and clear documentation can support research, healthcare, and quality in ways that matter. That is what led me toward laboratory work, where curiosity about how things work, together with the satisfaction of producing accurate results, has become the direction of my career. I am originally from Germany, and I hold a Doctorate from a university ranked in the global top 100. Through that academic path, I completed 4 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my interest in methodical, dependable work behind the scenes. One of my favourite family memories is coming home after a busy week in the lab and finding that my younger sibling had turned our kitchen into a “mini lab,” carefully labelling cups of juice like test samples; it was a funny but proud reminder that my enthusiasm for methodical work and discovery was visible to the people around me.

My background has also shaped how I approach technical work. In one role, I needed to use a new tool and became comfortable with it within a few weeks, using it productively in day-to-day work rather than treating it as a background exercise. On another occasion, I noticed that the team was repeatedly losing time searching through inconsistent records, so I introduced a simple tracking step that reduced repeated checking and saved time across the workflow. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas I have worked on before, and I value being able to help them move forward with clear answers and dependable results.

In addition, I have stayed with long stretches of work through several setbacks, including periods when deadlines required extra hours to keep records, samples, and records organized and on track. During one extended project, I stayed with the work through several obstacles and put in additional time where needed to carry it through to completion. Looking ahead, I am eager to bring this combination of scientific training, practical laboratory experience, and a genuine commitment to accurate, meaningful results to a Laboratory Technician role.
